alignments.note: Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary; discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).
Ethical dative `לְ` rendered as a bare indirect object *plant thee* (rule 40).
Noun with the indefinite article it licenses (rule 15).

`כֹּל` takes the *any* it is itself what the ASV renders by (rule 15), the *of* the ASV supplies before this appositional phrase, which goes to the word opening it (rule 33), and the generic *kind* supplied to expand the quantifier, which joins its unit and never heads it (rule 31). The relational *of* standing between the two nouns is the construct chain's own and belongs to the rectum (rule 19), exactly as `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` → *any of thy gates* is divided at DEU.16.5; keeping *of any kind of* whole was the accepted reading and is what this correction reverses.
Nomen rectum of `כָּל־עֵץ` takes the relational *of* together with its own word, headed on the noun (rule 19).
Construct noun with a supplied *the*; no article morpheme stands in the chain (rule 29).
Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary.
Ethical dative rendered as a bare indirect object (rule 40).

review_notes: Corrected at chapter reconciliation: the accepted alignment kept *of any kind of* whole on `כֹּל` and left `עֵץ` the bare *tree*. `כָּל־עֵץ` is an ordinary construct chain, so rule 19 puts the relational *of* on the nomen rectum and leaves the construct noun only what is written for it; the rule's `כֻּלָּם` paragraph is directly on point and forbids reading that *of* as part of an English quantifier. DEU.16.5 divides `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` → *any of thy gates* the same way.

The leading *of* at t008 is not the chain's relation and stays with `כֹּל`: `כָּל־עֵץ` stands in apposition to `אֲשֵׁרָה` with no preposition and no object marker on it, so rule 33 gives the supplied *of* to the word opening the phrase. The supplied generic *kind* joins the quantifier's unit under rule 31 and the head stays on *any*, the word carrying the lexeme.

DEU.16.4's `מִן־הַבָּשָׂר` → *any of the flesh* is not this construction and is unchanged: there the whole *any of* is the partitive preposition's under rule 24, because no construct relation stands in the phrase.
